QIRAAT-ER:12:43:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:12:43:4#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:12:43:4#1/r1.claim: The first-person yāʾ is vocalized in this canonical form but silent in the standard reading.
QIRAAT-ER:12:43:4#1/r1.anchor: Vocalized yāʾ al-mutakallim (ya al-idafa) vs. silent in standard reading; both canonical

QIRAAT-ER:12:43:24#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:12:43:24#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:12:43:24#1/r1.claim: Eliding hamza from ruʾyā yields rūyāya, a canonical phonological simplification without semantic change.
QIRAAT-ER:12:43:24#1/r1.anchor: Hamzless form: the hamza in رُؤْيَا is elided, yielding rūyāya

QIRAAT-ER:12:43:24#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:12:43:24#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:12:43:24#2/r1.claim: At pause, final yāʾ of the hamzless reading becomes sukūn.
QIRAAT-ER:12:43:24#2/r1.anchor: Pause form (waqf) of the hamzless reading — final yāʾ becomes sukūn

QIRAAT-ER:12:43:24#3/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:12:43:24#3/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:12:43:24#3/r1.claim: Assimilating the wāw of rū- to the following yāʾ yields ruyyāya without semantic change.
QIRAAT-ER:12:43:24#3/r1.anchor: the wāw of rū- assimilates to the following yāʾ producing ruyyāya — phonological but not semantic change

QIRAAT-ER:12:43:28#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:12:43:28#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:12:43:28#1/r1.claim: The hamzless form of al-ruʾyā elides hamza without changing meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:12:43:28#1/r1.anchor: Hamzless form of الرؤيا — elision of hamza; canonical in multiple readings; no semantic change

QIRAAT-ER:12:43:28#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:12:43:28#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:12:43:28#2/r1.claim: Assimilating wāw to yāʾ produces ruyyā, a phonological variant only.
QIRAAT-ER:12:43:28#2/r1.anchor: the wāw assimilates to yāʾ producing ruyyā — phonological variant only

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p279/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p279/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p279/r10.claim: The Egyptian king, named al-Rayyān ibn al-Walīd, sees seven fat cows from a dry river swallowed by seven lean cows, and seven ripe green ears overpowered by seven dry ones.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p279/r10.anchor: لما دنا فرج يوسف عليه السلام رأى ملك مصر الريان بن الوليد رؤيا عجيبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r1.claim: The present-tense أرى recounts a scene as if occurring now; أفتوني في رؤياي shows it is a dream.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r1.anchor: وأرى حكاية حال، فلذلك جاء بالمضارع دون رأيت

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r2.claim: Samān modifies the cows rather than the numeral, distinguishing a kind of cow; modifying the number itself would wrongly imply that the seven were fat.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r2.anchor: وسمان صفة لقوله: بقرات، ميز العدد بنوع من البقرات وهي السمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r3.claim: The distinction between ثلاث رجال كرام and ثلاثة رجال كرام shows that describing the counted subset differs from describing the people as a whole.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r3.anchor: وفرق بين قولك: عندي ثلاث رجال كرام، وثلاثة رجال كرام، لأن المعنى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r4.claim: Seven is not annexed to the adjective ajāf because numerals normally annex to adjectives only in poetry; exceptions are adjectives used as nouns, such as knights or companions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r4.anchor: ولم يضف سبع إلى عجاف لأن اسم العدد لا يضاف إلى الصفة إلا في الشعر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r5.claim: The mention of seven cows implies that the lean cows are also seven cows, with the counted noun omitted before their adjective.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r5.anchor: ودل قوله: سبع بقرات على أن السبع العجاف بقرات، كأنه قيل: سبع بقرات عجاف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r6.claim: The plural ajāf follows the opposite adjective samān, though the expected plural of ajfāʾ is ʿujuf, like khudr for khadrāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r6.anchor: وجاء جمع عجفاء على عجاف، وقياسه عجف كخضراء أو خضر، حملا على سمان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r7.claim: The division between fat and lean cows implies seven ears in each division; the numeral is omitted before أخر يابسات.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r7.anchor: والتقسيم في البقرات يقتضي التقسيم في السنبلات، فيكون قد حذف اسم العدد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r8.claim: أخر cannot be a genitive adjective of سنبلات خضر, since being another set makes it separate from the seven it would otherwise modify.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r8.anchor: ولا يصح أن يكون وأخر مجرورا عطفا على سنبلات خضر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r9.claim: Al-malaʾ are the king's leading officials who attend him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r9.anchor: والملأ: أشراف دولته وأعيانهم الذين يحضرون عند الملك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r10.speaker: أبو جعفر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r10.claim: Abū Jaʿfar assimilates the hamza in ruʾyā through an unusual sequence of sound changes; grammarians call it irregular because the waw substitution is optional.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r10.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر: بالإدغام في الرؤيا، وبابه بعد قلب الهمزة واوا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r11.claim: The lām in للرؤيا strengthens the verb's access to its object when the object precedes; it does not work as well when the object follows.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r11.anchor: واللام في الرؤيا مقوية لوصول الفعل إلى مفعوله إذا تقدم عليه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r12.claim: The apparent syntax makes تعبرون the predicate of كنتم.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r12.anchor: والظاهر أن خبر كنتم هو قوله: تعبرون

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r13.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r13.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī offers three more complex parses: الرؤيا as an explanatory topic with an omitted object, as predicate of كان with another predicate or circumstantial phrase, or as governed by an understood verb meaning undertake interpretation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r13.anchor: وأجاز الزمخشري فيه وجوها متكلفة أحدها: أن تكون الرؤيا للبيان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r14.claim: Dream interpretation is called عبور by analogy with crossing a river, as the interpreter reaches the vision's final meaning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p280/r14.anchor: وعبارة الرؤيا مأخوذة من عبر النهر إذا جازه من شط إلى شط

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p281/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p281/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p281/r6.claim: A poem cited by al-Mubarrad illustrates the use of the ungeminated verb ʿabara for interpreting a dream.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p281/r6.anchor: رأيت رؤيا ثم عبرتها ... وكنت للأحلام عبارا

FARRA:v2p46/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p46/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p46/r1.claim: The wording إني أرى is understood as a dream in Arabic; if the king meant waking observation he would state an ordinary action, and Abraham explicitly says he saw the vision in sleep.
FARRA:v2p46/r1.anchor: فعلم أنه للنوم ولو أراد الخبر لقال: إني أفعل إني أقوم

ALUSI-FULL:v12p248#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p248#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p248#2/r1.claim: The king is Rayyan, who was an unbeliever; his title illustrates the permissibility of calling an unbeliever king, though some prohibit king or amir for fear the title implies rightfulness, citing Muhammad's letter to Heraclius as 'great Roman'.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p248#2/r1.anchor: الريان وكان كافرا ففي إطلاق ذلك عليه دلالة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p248#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p248#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p248#2/r2.claim: The king's 'I see' means 'I saw'; the present tense vividly recounts the past vision.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p248#2/r2.anchor: أي رأيت وإيثار صيغة المضارع لحكاية الحال الماضية

ALUSI-FULL:v12p248#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p248#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p248#2/r3.claim: سمان describes cows full of flesh and fat; the plural can be regular as in كريم/كرام, and its lexical forms derive from samāna and samn.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p248#2/r3.anchor: ممتلئات لحما وشحما من سمن كسمع سمانة بالفتح وسمنا كعنبا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p248#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p248#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p248#2/r4.claim: The imperfect 'they eat' means that they ate, but makes the strange scene present to the listener; the clause is circumstantial or adjectival.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p248#2/r4.anchor: أي أكلهن والعدول إلى المضارع لاستحضار الصورة تعجيبا

ALUSI-FULL:v12p248#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p248#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p248#2/r5.claim: عجاف means very thin. Its plural is عجفاء, unusually patterned as عجاف rather than the expected عجف; it is formed in opposition to سمان.

ALUSI-FULL:v12p248#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p248#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p248#2/r6.claim: Describing the numeral's discriminator سمان rather than making it an adjective of the numeral better distinguishes by kind than gender and more fully removes ambiguity; a derived adjective is not a sound discriminator in formal usage.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p248#2/r6.anchor: وقد ذكروا أنه إذا وصف التمييز كان التمييز بالنوع وإذا وصف المميز كان التمييز بالجنس

ALUSI-FULL:v12p249/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249/r1.speaker: صاحب الفرائد
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249/r1.claim: The author of al-Fara'id objects that numeral discriminators normally appear in genitive construction: with seven lean, an omitted cows is needed, whereas adding lean could make the adjective stand for cows and avoid ellipsis.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249/r1.anchor: واعترض صاحب الفرائد بأن الأصل في العدد التمييز بالإضافة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p249/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249/r2.speaker: القطب
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249/r2.claim: Al-Qutb replies that the preceding mention of seven cows already identifies the lean seven as cows, so إضافة عجاف would make an adjective do the work of a discriminator; treating it as standing for cows applies only when it is an adjective.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249/r2.anchor: تعقب ذلك القطب بأنه هب أن الأصل في العدد التمييز بالإضافة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p249/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249/r3.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249/r3.claim: Al-Tibi says describing the number before its discriminator stresses both count and quality, while naming the discriminator first makes the description the focus; omission in all three parallel images serves the scene's movement from ease to hardship.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249/r3.anchor: إن المميز إذا وصف ثم رفع به الإبهام والإجمال من العدد آذن بأنهما مقصودان في الذكر

ALUSI-FULL:v12p249#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249#2/r1.claim: One explanation says the fat cows are named first because they appeared first: seven fat cows emerged from a dry river, then seven lean ones swallowed them without visibly changing.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249#2/r1.anchor: بأنه أول ما رأى السمان فقد روي أنه رأى سبع بقرات سمان خرجن من نهر يابس

ALUSI-FULL:v12p249#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249#2/r2.claim: The green ears had formed kernels and were green; the dry ears had ripened and curled until no green remained, according to a report. Their number is omitted because the earlier seven cows supply it.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249#2/r2.anchor: قد انعقد حبها واخضر أي وسبعا أخر

ALUSI-FULL:v12p249#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249#2/r3.claim: The author rejects coordinating أخر with سنبلات: the seven would then be both the green ears and a different set of dry ears, a numerical contradiction; coordination with a single set of seven men divided between standing and sitting is different.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249#2/r3.anchor: ولا يجوز عطف أخر على سنبلات لأن العطف على المميز يقتضي أن يكون المعطوف والمعطوف عليه بيانا للمعدود

ALUSI-FULL:v12p249#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249#2/r4.speaker: صاحب الفرائد
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249#2/r4.claim: Al-Fara'id argues coordination normally repeats the numeral: seven other ears would then be added to seven green ones, making fourteen; under the alternative ellipsis analysis the reading would instead wrongly make all ears total seven.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249#2/r4.anchor: ونظر في ذلك صاحب الفرائد فقال : إن الصحيح أن العطف في حكم تكرير العامل

ALUSI-FULL:v12p249#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249#2/r5.speaker: صاحب الفرائد
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249#2/r5.claim: Al-Fara'id further prefers coordinating with خضر rather than يابسات, so the dry description has an expressed ears noun and need not be supplied from context.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249#2/r5.anchor: وادعى أن الأولى أن يكون العطف

ALUSI-FULL:v12p249#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249#2/r6.claim: Al-Alusi says the objection still assumes a discriminator already fixed at seven; neither repetition nor ellipsis resolves that contradiction, and he prefers the ellipsis or 'withdrawal' analysis followed by Ibn al-Hajib.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249#2/r6.anchor: ومن ذلك يظهر أنه لا مدخل للتكرير ولا الإنسحاب في هذا الفرض ثم إن المختار قول الإنسحاب

ALUSI-FULL:v12p249#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249#2/r7.claim: The claim that أخر would be needless under an omitted seven is unsound: both competing grammatical analyses are recognized as apparent by Arab grammarians, so the word can emphasize the intended reading rather than be verbose.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249#2/r7.anchor: فغير سديد على ما في الكشف لأن القائل بالتقدير يدعي الظهور في الإستقلال

ALUSI-FULL:v12p249#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249#2/r8.claim: The address يا أيها الملأ is to notables thought to possess knowledge; one report says the king gathered magicians, soothsayers, and dream interpreters.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p249#2/r8.anchor: خطاب للأشراف ممن يظن به العلم يروى أنه جمع السحرة والكهنة والمعبرين

ALUSI-FULL:v12p250/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p250/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p250/r1.claim: The king asks them to interpret the dream and state its consequence; another view says he addresses his companions and calls the task a fatwa to honor them and magnify the vision.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p250/r1.anchor: أي عبروها وبينوا حكمها وما تؤول إليه من العاقبة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p250/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p250/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p250/r2.claim: Dream interpretation is the habitual passage from a seen dream-image to its corresponding external or inward reality; عبور means crossing, and تأويل names what the dream comes to.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p250/r2.anchor: وهي الإنتقال من الصورة المشاهدة في المنام إلى ما هي صورة ومثال لها

ALUSI-FULL:v12p250/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p250/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v12p250/r3.claim: The light form عبر الرؤيا is more established and forceful in linguistic usage than the doubled form; although some deny the latter, al-Mubarrad's Bedouin poem attests it.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p250/r3.anchor: عبرت الرؤيا بالتخفيف عبارة أقوى وأعرف عند أهل اللغة

ALUSI-FULL:v12p250/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p250/r4.speaker: المبرد
ALUSI-FULL:v12p250/r4.claim: Al-Mubarrad cites a Bedouin poet's line about seeing and interpreting a dream as evidence that the doubled verb تعبير is attested.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p250/r4.anchor: ما أنشده المبرد في الكامل لبعض الأعراب

ALUSI-FULL:v12p250/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p250/r5.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v12p250/r5.claim: Abu Hayyan takes the lām in للرؤيا as an emphatic or strengthening lām for a delayed weakened verb; other accounts call it explanatory, make it indicate eagerness to interpret, or treat الرؤيا as a predicate of كان, which Al-Alusi considers strained.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p250/r5.anchor: وقيل واختاره أبو حيان إنها لتقوية الفعل المذكور لأنه ضعف بالتأخير

ALUSI-FULL:v12p250/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v12p250/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر
ALUSI-FULL:v12p250/r6.claim: Abu Ja'far assimilates the hamza in الرؤيا after changing it to wāw and then yā because a preceding wāw is unvocalized; grammarians call this irregular because the wāw substitution is not obligatory.
ALUSI-FULL:v12p250/r6.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر بالإدغام في الرؤيا وبابه بعد قلب الهمزة واوا

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:43/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:43/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:43/r1.claim: As Joseph's release approached, the king dreamed of seven fat cows emerging from a dry river and seven emaciated cows swallowing them, along with green ears and dry ears; the latter overtook and overwhelmed the former.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:43/r1.anchor: لما دنا فرجه رأى الملك سبع بقرات سمان خرجن من نهر يابس

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:43/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:43/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:43/r2.claim: The green ears had formed grain, while the dry ones had ripened; their state is omitted because the cow imagery has already explained it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:43/r2.anchor: قد انعقد حبها. { وأخر يبست } وسبعا أخر يابسات

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:43/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:43/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:43/r3.claim: The feminine plural descriptors reflect how the first adjective distinguishes the cows and the second needs the noun to identify the sex; 'emaciated' is cast as the opposite of 'fat.'
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:43/r3.anchor: وأجرى السمان على المميز دون المميز لأن التمييز بها ووصف السبع الثاني بالعجاف

BAYDAWI-FULL:12:43/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:43/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:43/r4.claim: The king asks the council to interpret the dream; ta'bir is passage from imagined forms to their corresponding psychic meanings, and the lam either marks clarification, strengthens a delayed verb, or reflects a verb that takes lam.
BAYDAWI-FULL:12:43/r4.anchor: عبروها. { إن كنتم للرؤيا تعبرون } إن كنتم عالمين بعبارة الرؤيا

BIQAI-FULL:v4p46/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p46/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p46/r1.claim: When the forgotten request failed, God produced another cause for Joseph's elevation; the king is a powerful ruler responsible for politics and administration.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p46/r1.anchor: أثار الله سبحانه سببا ينفذ به ما أراد من رئاسته

BIQAI-FULL:v4p46/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p46/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p46/r2.claim: The king presents his vision to a court of elites, including sorcerers, priests, soothsayers, physiognomists, and sages, emphasizing that he is serious rather than testing them.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p46/r2.anchor: وهم السحرة والكهنة والحزرة والقافة والحكماء

BIQAI-FULL:v4p46/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p46/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p46/r3.claim: The present tense أرى narrates the vision as if unfolding now because it deeply alarmed the king; fat means bodily increase and عجاف means dry, emaciated thinness.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p46/r3.anchor: حكاية للحال لشدة ما هاله من ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v4p46/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p46/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p46/r4.claim: The dry ears overcome the green ears; the author says the number modifies a plural of paucity because the dream signifies famine and hardship, unlike the multiplied crop in 2:261.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p46/r4.anchor: ولما كان تأويل المنام الجدب والقحط والشدة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p46/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p46/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p46/r5.claim: A سنبلة is a reed-like plant bearing an ordered cluster of grains; the repeated seven is omitted from the second ears because the lean cattle already suggest it.

DURR-FULL:v4p503#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p503#2/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v4p503#2/r1.claim: The king's troubling dream showed seven fat cows eaten by seven lean cows and green ears eaten by dry ones; the assembled diviners called it confused dreams and admitted they could not interpret dreams.
DURR-FULL:v4p503#2/r1.anchor: ثم أن الله أرى الملك رؤيا في منامه هالته فرأى سبع بقرات سمان

DURR-FULL:v4p543/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p543/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v4p543/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the king's phrase أضغاث أحلام as false dreams; al-Dahhak agrees.
DURR-FULL:v4p543/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {أضغاث أحلام} قال: من الأحلام الكاذبة

DURR-FULL:v4p543/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p543/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v4p543/r3.claim: Mujahid glosses أضغاث أحلام as a mixture of dreams.
DURR-FULL:v4p543/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد - رضي الله عنه - في قوله {أضغاث أحلام} قال: أخلاط أحلام

DURR-FULL:v4p545/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v4p545/r5.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v4p545/r5.claim: Qatadah interprets the fat cows as fertile years, the lean cows as barren years, green ears as abundant harvests, and dry ears as drought.
DURR-FULL:v4p545/r5.anchor: عن قتادة - رضي الله عنه - في قوله {أفتنا في سبع بقرات} الآية قال: أما السمان فسنون

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2150/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2150/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2150/r1.claim: The king, Rayyan ibn al-Walid, saw a disturbing dream that he recognized as true but could not interpret, so he asked his court for an interpretation.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2150/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ثم ان الملك ريان بن الوليد ، راى الرؤيا التي هالته وعرف انها رؤيا واقعة ، ولم يدر ما تاويلها

IBNABIHATIM:v7p2150/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2150/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2150/r2.claim: God showed the king a troubling dream of seven fat cows eaten by seven lean cows and seven green ears eaten by dry ones; he consulted sorcerers, soothsayers, physiognomists, and bird augurs, who called it confused dreams and professed no knowledge.
IBNABIHATIM:v7p2150/r2.anchor: عن السدي : ثم ان الله تعالى ارى الملك رؤيا في منامه هالته ، فراى سبع بقرات سمان ياكلهن سبع عجاف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r1.claim: The seven ears are joined to the seven cows; the wording recalls the parable of a grain producing seven ears.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r1.anchor: و { وسبع سنبلات } معطوف على { سبع بقرات }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r2.claim: Al-malaʾ means the leading or distinguished people.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r3.claim: Iftāʾ is giving a fatwa or explanation, as discussed in the earlier prison scene.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r4.claim: The preposition fi figuratively marks an interpretation attached to the dream, like an explanation attached to something concise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r4.anchor: للظرفية المجازية التي هي بمعنى الملابسة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r5.claim: Putting “for the dream” before its verb observes the cadence and foregrounds the dream; its definite article is generic.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r5.anchor: للرعاية على الفاصلة مع الاهتمام بالرؤيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r6.claim: The lām reinforces the delayed verb's connection to its object; al-Zamakhshari says careful scholars prefer the light form ʿabara, not the doubled form.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r6.anchor: لام التقوية لضعف العامل عن العمل بالتأخير

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r7.claim: Ibn Ashur cites a verse recited by al-Mubarrad from an unnamed Bedouin as evidence for dream-interpreter wording: “I saw my dream, then interpreted it; I was an interpreter of dreams.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r7.anchor: على بيت أنشده المبرد في كتاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r8.claim: Dream interpretation was a practiced Egyptian science with priestly rules; both the prisoners' request and the king's consultation indicate that the court included interpreters.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r8.anchor: وكان الكهنة منهم يعدونه من علومهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r9.claim: The Torah says Pharaoh summoned Egyptian magicians and sages but found no interpreter; dream interpretation was associated with priests because it concerned the unseen.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r10.claim: Prophetic biography reports that Kisra sent for the soothsayer Satiḥ to interpret a dream around the Prophet's birth, counted among prophetic portents; Kisra was alarmed and sent Abd al-Masih.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v12p281/r10.anchor: أن كسرى أرسل إلى سطيح الكاهن

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247#3/r1.claim: The king says he sees the dream while describing a past dream, using the present because the vision is being contemplated now.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247#3/r1.anchor: إني أرى في المنام أني أذبحك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247#3/r2.claim: A report adds that seven thin cows emerged after the fat cows from a river and ate them, then disappeared inside their bellies.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247#3/r2.anchor: فرأيتها أكلت تلك السمان حتى حصلت في بطونها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247#3/r3.claim: ʿIjāf describes cows that have reached the extreme of emaciation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247#3/r3.anchor: التي بلغت غاية الهزال، ومنه قول الشاعر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247#3/r4.claim: A poet’s description of Meccan men as emaciated witnesses this meaning of عجاف.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247#3/r5.claim: Readers differ in pronouncing the two hamzas of أفتوني; another group pronounces an intervening alif as wāw.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247#3/r6.claim: The lām in للرؤيا links and emphasizes the fronted object; dream interpretation is named for crossing a river from one bank to another, as the interpreter reaches the dream’s endpoint.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p247#3/r6.anchor: من عبر النهر، وهو تجاوزه من شط إلى شط

SAMIN-DURR:12:43/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:43/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:43/r1.claim: سمان modifies بقرات; it is the plural of سمينة, while سمين can also form a shared-gender plural, like كرام.
SAMIN-DURR:12:43/r1.anchor: صفة لبقرات وهو جمع سمينة، ويجمع

SAMIN-DURR:12:43/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:43/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:43/r2.claim: سمن is the verbal noun and سمين the active adjective, both with irregular vowels compared with the expected pattern.
SAMIN-DURR:12:43/r2.anchor: فالمصدر واسم [الفاعل] جاءا على غير قياس

SAMIN-DURR:12:43/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:43/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:12:43/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains that describing the classifier بقرات selects a subtype of cows that are fat, while describing the numeral would first identify the number by cow-kind and then characterize it.
SAMIN-DURR:12:43/r3.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " هل من فرق بين إيقاع " سمان " صفة للمميز وهو " بقرات "

SAMIN-DURR:12:43/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:43/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:12:43/r4.claim: He says عجاف cannot be annexed directly as the numeral's discriminator because an adjective alone does not identify the counted kind; nouns like فرسان can act as nouns.
SAMIN-DURR:12:43/r4.anchor: والعجاف وصف لا يقع البيان به وحده.

SAMIN-DURR:12:43/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:43/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:43/r5.claim: An adjective on the genitive discriminator entails that the counted set has that quality, but a nominative adjective on the numeral does not necessarily describe the men.
SAMIN-DURR:12:43/r5.anchor: قلت: وهي أسئلة وأجوبة حسنة. وتحقيق السؤال الأول وجوابه: أنه يلزم من وصف التمييز بشيء

SAMIN-DURR:12:43#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#2/r1.claim: Number words are not normally annexed to adjectives; adjectives follow the number as nominative, with genitive attachment only in poetic necessity.
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#2/r1.anchor: وتحقيق الثاني وجوابه: أن أسماء العدد لا تضاف إلى الأوصاف إلا في ضرورة

SAMIN-DURR:12:43#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#2/r2.claim: Three huge ones is avoided because the described noun is unknown; here cows are known, but ordinary word order still makes direct annexation unnecessary.
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#2/r2.anchor: وتحقيق الثالث: أنه إنما امتنع " ثلاثة ضخام " ونحوه لأنه لا يعلم موصوفه

SAMIN-DURR:12:43#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#2/r3.claim: عجاف is the plural of عجفاء; the expected plural عجف is analogically leveled to سمان because the terms are opposites.
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#2/r3.anchor: وجمع عجفاء على عجاف. والقياس: عجف نحو: حمراء وحمر، حملا له على " سمان "

SAMIN-DURR:12:43#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#2/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#2/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari defines عجف as extreme emaciation and cites the line about Meccans in years of famine.
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#2/r4.anchor: قاله الزمخشري: " والعجف شدة الهزال الذي ليس بعده قال:

SAMIN-DURR:12:43#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#2/r5.speaker: الراغب
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#2/r5.claim: Al-Raghib relates عجف to a thin blade, aversion from food or a person, and encountering thin livestock.
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#2/r5.anchor: وقال الراغب: " هو من قولهم نصل أعجف، أي: دقيق، وعجفت نفسي عن الطعام

SAMIN-DURR:12:43#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#3/r1.claim: وأخر coordinates with سبع, not سنبلات; the omitted number is seven, understood from the matching groups of cows and ears.
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#3/r1.anchor: قوله: { وأخر } " أخر " نسق على " سبع " لا على " سنبلات "

SAMIN-DURR:12:43#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#3/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#3/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari infers that the dry ears are also seven because the passage repeatedly focuses on groups of seven.
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#3/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " فإن قلت: هل في الآية دليل على أن السنبلات اليابسة كانت سبعا كالخضر؟

SAMIN-DURR:12:43#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#3/r3.claim: Making أخر coordinate with سنبلات would both include the dry ears among the seven and exclude them as other ears, a contradiction; wording سبع سنبلات خضر ويابسات would allow a color division.
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#3/r3.anchor: وإنما لم يجز عطف " أخر " على التمييز وهو " سنبلات "

SAMIN-DURR:12:43#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#3/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#3/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhshari illustrates the contradiction with seven men described as standing and sitting versus seven standing and others sitting.
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#3/r4.anchor: فلو قلت: " عنده سبعة رجال قيام وآخرين قعود " تدافع ففسد

SAMIN-DURR:12:43#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#4/r1.claim: The lam in للرؤيا may be extra after fronting its object, strengthening its governing verb; such additions normally require fronting or a derived governor, with exceptions or a containment analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#4/r1.anchor: أحدها: أن اللام فيه مزيدة فلا تعلق لها بشيء، وزيدت لتقدم المعمول

SAMIN-DURR:12:43#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#4/r2.claim: Alternatively تعبرون may contain the meaning of a verb that takes lam: you undertake interpretation of the dream.
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#4/r2.anchor: الثاني: أن يضمن " تعبرون " معنى ما يتعدى باللام، تقديره: إن كنتم تنتدبون لعبارة الرؤيا

SAMIN-DURR:12:43#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#4/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#4/r3.claim: الرؤيا may be the predicate of كنتم, meaning capable of the task; تعبرون may then be a second predicate or a circumstantial clause.
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#4/r3.anchor: الثالث: أن يكون " للرؤيا " هو خبر " كنتم " كما تقول: " كان فلان لهذا الأمر "

SAMIN-DURR:12:43#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#4/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#4/r4.claim: The lam may clarify the intended object, as in يوسف 12:20; تقديره أعني للرؤيا, with the object of تعبرون omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#4/r4.anchor: الرابع: أن تتعلق اللام بمحذوف على أنها للبيان كقوله تعالى: وكانوا فيه من الزاهدين

SAMIN-DURR:12:43#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#4/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#4/r5.claim: Abu Ja'far reads الرؤيا as الريا by assimilation after replacing hamza with wāw; the author calls it weak because the replacement is not obligatory.
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#4/r5.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر " الرؤيا " وبابها " الريا " بالإدغام

SAMIN-DURR:12:43#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#4/r6.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#4/r6.claim: Al-Zamakhshari endorses the light form عبرت and says authoritative speakers reject the doubled form عبرت, التعبير, and المعبر.
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#4/r6.anchor: وعبرت الرؤيا بالتخفيف قال الزمخشري: " هو الذي اعتمده الأثبات

SAMIN-DURR:12:43#4/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#4/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#4/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari adduces an Arab poem containing عبارا as evidence for the heavier noun form and explains crossing a dream as stating its eventual outcome.
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#4/r7.anchor: وقد عثرت على بيت أنشده المبرد في كتاب " الكامل " لبعض الأعراب

SAMIN-DURR:12:43#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#5/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#5/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says interpreting a dream is called crossing it because one describes its outcome, as crossing a river means reaching the far side.
SAMIN-DURR:12:43#5/r1.anchor: قال: " وحقيقة عبرت الرؤيا: ذكرت عاقبتها وآخر أمرها كما تقول: عبرت النهر إذا قطعته

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p229/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p229/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p229/r1.claim: The king is the chief king of Egypt; “I see” is in the present tense but can mean that he saw the dream.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p229/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى ( وقال الملك ) يعني ملك مصر الأكبر ( إني أرى ) يعني في المنام

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p229/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p229/r2.speaker: وهب بن منبه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p229/r2.claim: Wahb says that when Joseph's appointed prison term ended, Gabriel announced his release, kingship, and reunion with his father; that night the king dreamed of cows and grain.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p229/r2.anchor: لما انقضت المدة التي وقتها الله تعالى ليوسف في حبسه دخل عليه جبريل إلى السجن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p229/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p229/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p229/r3.claim: The seven thin cows had reached the extreme of emaciation; the “council” are people consulted and followed in decisions.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p229/r3.anchor: والعجاف التي قد بلغت في الهزال الغاية والملأ الذين يرجع إليهم في الأمور ويقتدى برأيهم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p229/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p229/r4.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p229/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the lām in “for the dream” clarifies the object: “if you interpret dreams.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p229/r4.anchor: واللام في قوله ( للرؤيا ) دخلت على المفعول للتبيين المعنى إن كنتم تعبرون

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p229/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p229/r5.speaker: ابن الأنباري
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p229/r5.claim: Ibn al-Anbari gives two functions for the lām: emphasis or the sense “toward,” directing the interpretation to the dream.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p229/r5.anchor: أحدهما أنها للتوكيد والثاني أنها أفادت معنى إلى والمعنى إن كنتم توجهون العبارة إلى الرؤيا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p229/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p229/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p229/r6.claim: Interpreting a dream means telling the outcome toward which its matter will turn; the word is derived from crossing to a riverbank.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p229/r6.anchor: ومعنى عبرت الرؤيا وعبرتها أخبرت بآخر ما يؤول إليه أمرها واشتقاقه من عبر النهر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r1.claim: As Yusuf's release neared, Egypt's king Rayyan ibn al-Walid saw seven fat cows eaten by seven lean cows and seven ripe green ears overcome by seven dry ears, but found no interpreter.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r1.anchor: لما دنا فرج يوسف ، رأى ملك مصر ( الريان بن الوليد ) رؤيا عجيبة هالته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r2.claim: Making fat an adjective of cows distinguishes the seven by a type of cow, whereas making it describe seven would distinguish by genus before adding the quality.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r2.anchor: قلت : إذا أوقعتها صفة لبقرات . فقد قصدت إلى أن تميز السبع بنوع من البقرات

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r3.claim: The word ʿijāf cannot alone specify a count's genus; substantivized adjectives such as horsemen or companions can serve as classifiers, unlike mere adjectives.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r3.anchor: والعجاف وصف لا يقع البيان به وحده

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r4.claim: The dry ears are also seven: the context's count governs cows and green ears, and the word ukhar means seven others.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r4.anchor: فوجب أن يتناول معنى الأخر السبع ، ويكون قوله : { وأخر يابسات } بمعنى وسبعا أخر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r5.claim: Coordinating dry ears as a genitive adjective of the green ears would conflict with ukhar, which requires them to be other than the seven.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r5.anchor: ولفظ الأخر يقتضي أن تكون غير السبع

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r6.claim: The addressed council comprises leading scholars and sages.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r6.anchor: كأنه أراد الأعيان من العلماء والحكماء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r7.claim: The lam in lil-ruʾyā may explain the object, compensate when an object precedes its verb, mark competence as a predicate, or accompany an understood verb of volunteering.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r7.anchor: واللام في قوله { للرؤيا } إما أن تكون للبيان ، كقوله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r8.claim: The basic sense of interpreting a dream is to state its end or outcome, like crossing a river to reach its far side; taʾwīl likewise names its destination.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r8.anchor: وحقيقة ( عبرت الرؤيا ) ذكرت عاقبتها وآخر أمرها ، كما تقول : عبرت النهر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r9.claim: The light form ʿabartu is the form trusted authorities use; he says they reject the doubled form, taʿbīr, and muʿabbir.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p446#2/r9.anchor: وعبرت الرؤيا بالتخفيف ، هو الذي اعتمده الأثبات ، ورأيتهم ينكرون ( عبرت )

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p41/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p41/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p41/r1.claim: The king who saw the dream was al-Walid ibn al-Rayan.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p41/r1.anchor: وهذه الرؤيا رآها الملك الأكبر الوليد بن الريان

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p41/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p41/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p41/r2.claim: The dream both became the means of Joseph's release and warned of drought, allowing people to prepare.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p41/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p41/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p41/r3.claim: Because the king did not know the dream's interpretation, he announced it to his people so anyone with interpretive knowledge could hear and explain it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p41/r3.anchor: وذلك أن الملك لما لم يعلم تأويل رؤياه نادى بها في قومه ليسمع بها من يكون عنده علم بتأويلها فيعبرها له

MUJAHID:v1p316#2/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p316#2/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p316#2/r1.claim: Mujahid says Joseph asked the released prisoner to mention him to the king; the prisoner forgot until the king dreamed. Satan made Joseph forget remembrance of his Lord and direct his plea to the king, so Joseph remained imprisoned for years because he had said to mention him to the king.
MUJAHID:v1p316#2/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد ﴿ وقال للذي ظن أنه ناج منهما اذكرني عند ربك ﴾ يوسف يقول هذا للذي نجا من السجن

NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#3/r1.claim: The Egyptian king al-Rayyan ibn al-Walid dreamed of seven fat cows eaten by seven lean ones and seven green ears overcome by seven dry ears; the unusual vision distressed him.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#3/r1.anchor: رأى الملك مصر الريان بن الوليد رؤيا عجيبة هالته

NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#3/r2.claim: Joseph's ordeal began with a dream and his deliverance also came through one.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#3/r2.anchor: وقيل كان ابتداء بلاء يوسف فى الرؤيا ثم كان سبب نجاته أيضا الرؤيا

NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#3/r3.claim: Sīmān is a regular plural of fat; ʿijāf is a plural of lean, an unusual pattern for feminine afʿal adjectives, modeled on its opposite sīmān by pairing opposites.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#3/r3.anchor: والعجاف المهازيل والعجف الهزال الذى ليس بعده سمانه

NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#3/r4.claim: Although only the green ears are explicitly numbered, the structure repeatedly centers on seven, so the dry ears also number seven.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#3/r4.anchor: وفى الآية دلالة على أن سنبلات اليابسة كانت سبعا كالخضر

NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#3/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#3/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#3/r5.claim: Al-malāʾ means the realm's prominent scholars and sages.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#3/r5.anchor: كأنه أراد الأعيان من العلماء والحكماء

NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#3/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#3/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#3/r6.claim: The lām in li-l-ruʾyā may clarify, reinforce a fronted object that is weaker in governing the verb, or form a predicate of kāna; taʿburūn can be another predicate or a circumstantial clause.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#3/r6.anchor: اللام فى للرؤيا للبيان كقوله وكانوا فيه من الزاهدين

NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#3/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#3/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#3/r7.claim: To interpret a dream is to state its outcome, like crossing a river to its far bank; taʾwīl likewise names its end or return.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#3/r7.anchor: وحقيقة عبرت الرؤيا ذكرت عاقبتها وأخر أمرها كما تقول عبرت النهر

NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#3/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#3/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#3/r8.claim: The light form ʿabartu is the established reading; the source says scholars reject the heavy form, taʿbīr, and muʿabbir.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p190#3/r8.anchor: بالتخفيف هو الذى اعتمده الإثبات ورأيتهم ينكرون عبرت بالتشديد

ZAJJAJ:v3p112/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p112/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p112/r1.claim: ʿIjāf are cows that have reached the extreme of emaciation; the malāʾ are people consulted whose opinions are followed.
ZAJJAJ:v3p112/r1.anchor: العجاف التي قد بلغت في الهزال الغاية والنهاية.

ZAJJAJ:v3p112/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p112/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p112/r2.claim: The lām in li-l-ruʾyā marks the object and clarifies ‘interpret’; ʿabara a dream means report its eventual outcome, by analogy with crossing to the far bank.
ZAJJAJ:v3p112/r2.anchor: هذه اللام أدخلت على المفعول لتبين المعنى

QURTUBI-FULL:12:43/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43/r1.claim: As Joseph's release neared, Gabriel told him the king's dream would bring freedom and power; the account identifies the king as al-Rayyan ibn al-Walid and describes seven fat cows from a dry river eaten by seven lean cows and green ears consumed by dry ears.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43/r1.anchor: لما دنا فرج يوسف عليه السلام رأى الملك رؤياه، فنزل جبريل فسلم على يوسف وبشره

QURTUBI-FULL:12:43/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43/r2.claim: The king was frightened and consulted courtiers and experts in divination, astrology, soothsaying, and magic; they dismissed his vision as mixed dreams.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43/r2.anchor: فأرسل إلى الناس وأهل العلم منهم والبصر بالكهانة والنجامة والعرافة والسحر، وأشراف قومه

QURTUBI-FULL:12:43/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43/r3.speaker: عطاء
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj reports Ata's view that confused dreams are false or mistaken visions.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43/r3.anchor: قال ابن جريج قال لي عطاء: إن أضغاث الأحلام الكاذبة المخطئة من الرؤيا

QURTUBI-FULL:12:43/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43/r4.speaker: الضحاك عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43/r4.claim: Al-Dahhak, from Ibn Abbas, says some dreams are true and some are confused, meaning false.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43/r4.anchor: وقال جويبر عن الضحاك عن ابن عباس قال: إن الرؤيا منها حق، ومنها أضغاث أحلام

QURTUBI-FULL:12:43/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43/r5.speaker: الهروي
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43/r5.claim: Al-Harawi glosses أضغاث as mixed dreams, from the word for a bundle of plants or grass, hence a muddled vision.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43/r5.anchor: وقال الهروي: قوله تعالى: { أضغاث أحلام } أي أخلاط أحلام. والضغث في اللغة الحزمة من الشيء

QURTUBI-FULL:12:43/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43/r6.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43/r6.claim: Mujahid says confused dreams are frightening jumble and terrors.

QURTUBI-FULL:12:43/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43/r7.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43/r7.claim: Abu Ubayda defines confused dreams as visions with no interpretation.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43/r7.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: الأضغاث ما لا تأويل له من الرؤيا

QURTUBI-FULL:12:43/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43/r8.claim: The feminine numeral سبع precedes feminine بقرات; سمان is an adjective of cows, though outside Quranic wording it could describe the numeral, like the cited construction in 67:3.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43/r8.anchor: حذفت الهاء من «سبع» فرقا بين المذكر والمؤنث «سمان» من نعت البقرات

QURTUBI-FULL:12:43#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43#2/r1.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43#2/r1.claim: Ali says fat cattle in a town signal prosperous years, and lean cattle harsh years; in a coastal town during sailing season they may signal arriving ships, otherwise successive turmoil resembling cattle faces.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43#2/r1.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه: المعز والبقر إذا دخلت المدينة فإن كانت

QURTUBI-FULL:12:43#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43#2/r2.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43#2/r2.claim: In Ali's interpretation, uniformly yellow cattle can mean disease; different colors, ugly horns, or fire and smoke from their mouths can signify an army, raid, or attacking enemy.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43#2/r2.anchor: إلا أن تكون صفرا كلها فإنها أمراض تدخل على الناس، وإن كانت مختلفة الألوان، شنيعة

QURTUBI-FULL:12:43#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43#2/r3.claim: A cow may also symbolize a wife, servant, crop yield, or year because it bears offspring and produces yield and vegetation.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43#2/r3.anchor: وقد تدل البقرة على الزوجة والخادم والغلة والسنة لما يكون فيها من الولد والغلة والنبات

QURTUBI-FULL:12:43#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43#2/r4.claim: عجاف is parsed from either of two cited verb patterns, عَجَفَ يَعْجَفُ or عَجِفَ يَعْجَفُ.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43#2/r4.anchor: من عجف يعجف، على وزن عظم يعظم، وروي عجف يعجف على وزن حمد يحمد

QURTUBI-FULL:12:43#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43#2/r5.claim: أفتوني في رؤياي means tell me the ruling or interpretation of my dream; ʿibārah derives from crossing a river, as an interpreter crosses toward the dream's outcome.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43#2/r5.anchor: فعابر، الرؤيا يعبر بما يؤول إليه أمرها

QURTUBI-FULL:12:43#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43#2/r6.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43#2/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the lām in للرؤيا clarifies the object: if you interpret, namely, the dream.
QURTUBI-FULL:12:43#2/r6.anchor: واللام في «للرؤيا» للتبيين، أي إن كنتم تعبرون، ثم بين فقال: للرؤيا، قاله الزجاج

RAZI-FULL:v18p118/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p118/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p118/r1.claim: As Joseph's release approached, the Egyptian king dreamed of seven fat cows eaten by seven lean cows and seven green ears overgrown by seven dry ones; his advisers called it confused and un-interpretable.
RAZI-FULL:v18p118/r1.anchor: رأى ملك مصر في النوم سبع بقرات سمان خرجن من نهر يابس وسبع بقرات عجاف

RAZI-FULL:v18p118/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p118/r2.speaker: الليث
RAZI-FULL:v18p118/r2.claim: Al-Layth defines ʿajaf as loss of fat and notes that ʿajaf is an anomalous plural matching the opposite word simān by analogy.
RAZI-FULL:v18p118/r2.anchor: قال الليث : العجف ذهاب السمن والفعل عجف يعجف

RAZI-FULL:v18p118/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p118/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p118/r3.claim: Some grammarians treat the lām in للرؤيا as extra because the object precedes its verb; al-Zamakhshari instead allows الرؤيا to be a predicate of kāna, with تعبرون as another predicate or a circumstantial phrase.
RAZI-FULL:v18p118/r3.anchor: على قول البعض زائدة لتقدم المفعول على الفعل

RAZI-FULL:v18p118/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p118/r4.speaker: الأزهري
RAZI-FULL:v18p118/r4.claim: Al-Azhari derives dream interpretation from crossing a river: the interpreter considers the two sides of a dream and moves from images to their meaning.
RAZI-FULL:v18p118/r4.anchor: وحكى الأزهري أن هذا مأخوذ من العبر

RAZI-FULL:v18p118/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p118/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p118/r5.claim: A confused dream is like a bundle of mixed plants; if its elements lack proportion or relation, it resembles a bundle of disparate things.
RAZI-FULL:v18p118/r5.anchor: والأضغاث جمع الضغث وهو الحزمة من أنواع النبت والحشيش

RAZI-FULL:v18p118#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v18p118#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v18p118#2/r1.claim: The advisers did not deny that dream interpretation exists; they said the king's vision was an incoherent mixture beyond their skill, while implying a more accomplished interpreter might understand it.
RAZI-FULL:v18p118#2/r1.anchor: القوم ما نفوا عن أنفسهم كونهم عالمين بعلم التعبير

ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.claim: Unlike Genesis' romantic account of Joseph's fortunes, the Qur'anic story illustrates God's unfathomable direction of human affairs: people may hate what is good for them or love what is bad for them.
ASAD-NOTES:12:intro/r2.anchor: the Qur'an uses it primarily as an illustration of God's unfathomable direction of men's affairs

ASAD-NOTES:12:43#n44/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:12:43#n44/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:12:43#n44/r1.claim: Asad identifies the king as probably a Hyksos ruler and argues their Arab origins and kinship with Hebrews explain his confidence in Joseph and the later Israelite settlement in Egypt.
ASAD-NOTES:12:43#n44/r1.anchor: This king seems to have been one of the six Hyksos rulers who dominated Egypt

STUDYQURAN:12:43/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:43/r1.speaker: Kl and JJ
STUDYQURAN:12:43/r1.claim: The notables were high-ranking members of the king’s entourage, and he asked them to interpret his dream.
STUDYQURAN:12:43/r1.anchor: high offices in his kingdom (Kl), to give him their opinion means that he wanted them to interpret the dream for him (JJ)

STUDYQURAN:12:43/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:43/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:12:43/r2.claim: Visions here means true or veridical dreams, as discussed at 12:4.
STUDYQURAN:12:43/r2.anchor: By visions here are meant true or veridical dreams (see 12:4c).

STUDYQURAN:12:43/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:43/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:12:43/r3.claim: The verb ʿabara comes from ʿ-b-r, meaning to cross from one side to another; in dream interpretation it describes moving from symbolic dream forms to their actual meanings.
STUDYQURAN:12:43/r3.anchor: moving from the imaginal and symbolic forms in dreams to the actual meanings they symbolize (Bḍ)

STUDYQURAN:12:43/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:12:43/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:12:43/r4.claim: The king’s dream is interpreted in 12:47–49.
STUDYQURAN:12:43/r4.anchor: For the interpretation of the king’s dream, see vv. 47–49 (cf. Genesis 41:1–8).

TAB-FULL:v13p177#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p177#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p177#2/r1.claim: Although the verse does not explicitly say the king was asleep, Arabs understand 'I see myself doing this' as reporting a dream; seven fat cows, seven lean cows, and ears of grain are therefore a dream vision.
TAB-FULL:v13p177#2/r1.anchor: عن السدي، قال: " إن الله أرى الملك في منامه رؤيا هالته، فرأى سبع بقرات سمان

TAB-FULL:v13p177#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p177#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v13p177#2/r2.claim: Al-Tabari glosses the seven green ears as dreamt ears, others as seven other ears, the mala' as nobles and associates, and aftuni as 'interpret it for me.'

TAB-FULL:v13p177#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p177#2/r3.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v13p177#2/r3.claim: Al-Suddi says God showed the king a frightening dream, after which he gathered diviners and interpreters; they called it confused dreams and admitted they could not interpret it.
TAB-FULL:v13p177#2/r3.anchor: عن السدي، قال: " إن الله أرى الملك في منامه رؤيا هالته، فرأى سبع بقرات سمان

TAB-FULL:v13p177#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v13p177#2/r4.speaker: ابن إسحاق
TAB-FULL:v13p177#2/r4.claim: Ibn Ishaq names the king as al-Rayyan ibn al-Walid and says he recognized the vision as true but did not know its interpretation.
TAB-FULL:v13p177#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن إسحاق، قال: " ثم إن الملك الريان بن الوليد رأى رؤياه التي رأى، فهالته

TABATABAI:12:43/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:43/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:43/r1.claim: The passage recounts Joseph’s release, rise in Egypt, and the king’s renewed investigation that fully establishes his innocence.
TABATABAI:12:43/r1.anchor: تتضمن الآيات قصة خروجه عليه السلام من السجن ونيله عزة مصر

TABATABAI:12:43/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:43/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:43/r2.claim: The king reports his own dream to the officials; the wording may describe a repeated dream, as with the earlier prisoners’ dreams.
TABATABAI:12:43/r2.anchor: رؤيا للملك يخبر بها الملأ والدليل عليه

TABATABAI:12:43/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:43/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:43/r3.claim: Saman means fat and ʿijaf means emaciated; the latter is an exceptional feminine adjective plural, with ʿujuf offered as its regular plural.
TABATABAI:12:43/r3.anchor: والسمان جمع سمينة والعجاف جمع عجفاء بمعنى المهزولة

TABATABAI:12:43/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:43/r4.speaker: المجمع
TABATABAI:12:43/r4.claim: Al-Majma defines fatwa as an answer about a ruling, though it may answer about the matter itself and then is not technically a fatwa.
TABATABAI:12:43/r4.anchor: قال في المجمع الفتيا الجواب عن حكم المعنى وقد يكون الجواب عن نفس المعنى

TABATABAI:12:43/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:43/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:43/r5.claim: Taʿbir comes from crossing: the interpreter passes from the dream’s familiar image to the reality represented beyond it.
TABATABAI:12:43/r5.anchor: وهو على أي حال مأخوذ من عبور النهر ونحوه كأن العابر يعبر من الرؤيا إلى ما وراءها

TABATABAI:12:43/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:43/r6.speaker: الكشاف
TABATABAI:12:43/r6.claim: Al-Kashshaf explains that fat qualifies the cows rather than the numeral to distinguish the seven by a kind of cow; making it describe the numeral would distinguish by species and then add a second description.
TABATABAI:12:43/r6.anchor: إذا أوقعتها صفة لبقرات فقد قصدت إلى أن تميز السبع بنوع من البقرات

TABATABAI:12:43/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:43/r7.speaker: الكشاف
TABATABAI:12:43/r7.claim: Al-Kashshaf says the dry ears must also number seven because the passage centers on seven cows and seven green ears; coordinating dry ears as a subset would conflict with the word others.
TABATABAI:12:43/r7.anchor: الكلام مبني على انصبابه إلى هذا العدد في البقرات السمان والعجاف والسنابل الخضر

TABATABAI:12:49#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:49#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:49#2/r1.claim: The dream depicts the practical measures the king must take for a coming famine: repeated planting, preserving grain in ears, and rationing reserves, rather than simply forecasting years.
TABATABAI:12:49#2/r1.anchor: أن الذي رآه الملك من الرؤيا إنما كان مثال ما يجب عليه من اتخاذ التدبير لإنجاء الناس من مصيبة الجدب

TABATABAI:12:49#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:49#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:49#2/r2.claim: Cows represent yearly provisions: fat cows picture plentiful harvests from sustained planting, lean cows picture shortages, and their eating the fat ones pictures famine consuming saved food.
TABATABAI:12:49#2/r2.anchor: فحكت السنين المخصبة والمجدبة أي الرزق الذي يرتزقون به فيها في صورة البقرة

TABATABAI:12:49#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:49#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:49#2/r3.claim: The green ears represent stores to be saved and the dry ears indicate preserving grain unthreshed; the dream shows the work required to protect food supplies.
TABATABAI:12:49#2/r3.anchor: وحكت ما يجب عليهم في حفظ ذخائر الرزق بالسنبلات اليابسة قبال السنبلات الخضر

TABATABAI:12:49#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:49#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:49#3/r3.claim: The dry ears are not expressly numbered because the dream depicts duties for famine management, not the famine years themselves; numbering would be needed under a forecast reading.
TABATABAI:12:49#3/r3.anchor: ومما ذكرنا أيضا تظهر النكتة في ترك توصيف السنبلات اليابسة

TABATABAI:12:93-102#13/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:93-102#13/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:93-102#13/r2.claim: The Qur'an also recounts Joseph's dream, his prison companions' dreams, and Pharaoh's dream.
TABATABAI:12:93-102#13/r2.anchor: ومنها ما حكاه تعالى من رؤيا يوسف عليه السلام إذ قال يوسف لأبيه يا أبت إني رأيت

TABATABAI:12:93-102#14/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:93-102#14/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:93-102#14/r1.claim: European natural scientists generally deny that dreams are real or scientifically connected to external events, while some psychologists study them; authentic dreams disclose future events or hidden facts in ways chance cannot explain.
TABATABAI:12:93-102#14/r1.anchor: الباحثين من علماء الطبيعة من أوربا لا يرون لها حقيقة

TABATABAI:12:93-102#15/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:93-102#15/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:93-102#15/r1.claim: Everyone has encountered dreams that reveal hidden matters or future events, especially clear dreams requiring no interpretation; their correspondence to later events cannot be dismissed as coincidence.
TABATABAI:12:93-102#15/r1.anchor: ما منا واحد إلا وقد شاهد من نفسه شيئا من الرؤى والمنامات دله على بعض الأمور الخفية

TABATABAI:12:93-102#15/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:93-102#15/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:93-102#15/r2.claim: Dreaming is a mental act involving imagination, which recombines stored sensory images; bodily conditions, temperament, and emotions shape many ordinary dreams.
TABATABAI:12:93-102#15/r2.anchor: والمتخيلة من القوى الفعالة دائما ربما تدوم في عملها من جهة الأنباء الواردة عليها من ناحية الحس

TABATABAI:12:93-102#15/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:93-102#15/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:93-102#15/r3.claim: Naturalist critics correctly identify bodily and emotional causes that shape many dreams, but their account only shows that some dreams lack truth.
TABATABAI:12:93-102#15/r3.anchor: وهذا هو الذي ذكره منكروا حقيقة الرؤيا من علماء الطبيعة لا يزيد على تعداد هذه الأسباب

TABATABAI:12:93-102#15/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:93-102#15/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:93-102#15/r4.claim: The claim that every dream is unreal does not follow: some sound dreams reveal truths and have a real relation to external events.
TABATABAI:12:93-102#15/r4.anchor: وهو غير المدعى وهو أن كل منام ليس ذا حقيقة فإن هناك منامات صالحة ورؤيا صادقة

TABATABAI:12:93-102#16/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:93-102#16/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:93-102#16/r1.claim: Every dream has causes and thus an interpretation, but causes vary: bodily or temperamental influences, chance circumstances, and preoccupations can produce dreams without foretelling external events.
TABATABAI:12:93-102#16/r1.anchor: فقد ظهر مما بينا أن جميع الرؤى لا تخلو عن حقيقة بمعنى أن هذه الإدراكات المتنوعة المختلفة

TABATABAI:12:93-102#16/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:93-102#16/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:93-102#16/r2.claim: The relevant true dreams are those not caused by external bodily or accidental factors, nor internal dispositions, yet connected to external events and cosmic realities.
TABATABAI:12:93-102#16/r2.anchor: وإنما البحث في نوع واحد من هذه المنامات

TABATABAI:12:93-102#16/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:93-102#16/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:93-102#16/r3.claim: Because future or hidden events are absent from the dreamer's senses, the author proposes that the sleeping soul connects to their causes beyond the physical world.
TABATABAI:12:93-102#16/r3.anchor: ولذا قيل إن الارتباط إنما استقر بينها وبين النفس النائمة من جهة اتصال النفس بسبب الحادثة الواقعة

TABATABAI:12:93-102#16/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:93-102#16/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:93-102#16/r4.claim: He distinguishes the physical world of changing matter, the imaginal world of immaterial forms that causes physical events, and the intellectual world of universal truths that causes the imaginal realm.
TABATABAI:12:93-102#16/r4.anchor: أن العوالم ثلاثة عالم الطبيعة وهو العالم الدنيوي الذي نعيش فيه والأشياء الموجودة فيها صور مادية

TABATABAI:12:93-102#17/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:93-102#17/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:93-102#17/r1.claim: A soul able to grasp intellectual realities may see universal causes directly; otherwise it represents them through familiar images, and a sound soul may perceive causes without alteration in a clear dream.
TABATABAI:12:93-102#17/r1.anchor: فإن كانت النفس كاملة متمكنة من إدراك المجردات العقلية أدركتها واستحضرت أسباب الكائنات

TABATABAI:12:93-102#17/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:93-102#17/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:93-102#17/r2.claim: Other true dreams use symbols or opposites, such as a crown for honor or darkness for ignorance; these require interpretation by returning each image to the reality first perceived.
TABATABAI:12:93-102#17/r2.anchor: وهذه هي التي تحتاج إلى التعبير بردها إلى الأصل الذي هو المشهود الأولى للنفس كرد التاج إلى الفخار

TABATABAI:12:93-102#17/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:93-102#17/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:93-102#17/r3.claim: Symbolic dreams divide into manageable transformations and tangled sequences of transformations; the latter are confused dreams that resist interpretation, unlike clear dreams and interpretable symbolic dreams.
TABATABAI:12:93-102#17/r3.anchor: المنامات التي تصرفت فيها النفس بالحكاية والتمثيل

TABRISI:12:43-49/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:43-49/r5.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
TABRISI:12:43-49/r5.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Muhammad reads سبع سنابل rather than the form used in the verse text.
TABRISI:12:43-49/r5.anchor: وقرأ جعفر بن محمد عليهما السلام وسبع سنابل

TABRISI:12:43-49#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:43-49#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:43-49#2/r1.claim: Dreams may come from God or angels and admit interpretation, from Satan without interpretation, or from the sleeper's beliefs and prior thoughts.
TABRISI:12:43-49#2/r1.anchor: منها ما يكون من الله تعالى وملائكته وهو الذي له تعبير وتأويل

TABRISI:12:43-49#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:43-49#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:43-49#2/r2.claim: ʿAjaf denotes loss of fat; aʿjaf and ʿajfāʾ are the masculine and feminine forms, with ʿijāf as an unusual plural.
TABRISI:12:43-49#2/r2.anchor: والعجف ذهاب السمن والذكر أعجف والأنثى عجفاء

TABRISI:12:44-46/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:44-46/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:44-46/r4.claim: The king was the Egyptian ruler al-Walid ibn Rayyan, and al-ʿAziz was his minister; the majority understand the vision as occurring in sleep.
TABRISI:12:44-46/r4.anchor: ملك مصر وهو الوليد بن ريان والعزيز وزيره وفيما رواه الأكثرون إني أرى في منامي

TABRISI:12:44-46/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:44-46/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:44-46/r5.claim: The seven lean cows consume the fat ones until they disappear; the dry ears curl over and overcome the green ears.
TABRISI:12:44-46/r5.anchor: فدخلت السمان في بطون المهازيل حتى لم أر منهن شيئا

TABRISI:12:44-46/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:12:44-46/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:12:44-46/r6.claim: The king addresses the elite; another view says the assembly was magicians and soothsayers.
TABRISI:12:44-46/r6.anchor: جمع الأشراف. وقيل: جمع السحرة والكهنة

THALABI:v5p225/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p225/r5.speaker: الكلبي
THALABI:v5p225/r5.claim: Al-Kalbi says the seven years of this imprisonment came after five earlier years; as release approached, the Egyptian king dreamed of seven fat cows consumed by seven lean ones.
THALABI:v5p225/r5.anchor: قال الكلبي- وهذه السبعة سوى الخمسة التي كانت قبل ذلك

THALABI:v5p225/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p225/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p225/r6.claim: The king also saw seven green ears and seven dry ones and summoned the elite to interpret the dream.
THALABI:v5p225/r6.anchor: وأرى سبع سنبلات خضر قد انعقد حبها وسبعا أخر يابسات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p126/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p126/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p126/r1.claim: The king saw seven fat cows swallowed by seven lean cows until none remained visible, and seven ripe green ears overcome by seven dry ears; he asked his court to interpret it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p126/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون (¬2): لما ذكرنا فرج يوسف، رأى ملك مصر الأكبر رؤيا عجيبة هالته،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p126/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p126/r2.speaker: الليث
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p126/r2.claim: عجف means loss of fat; عجاف describes thin animals with no flesh or fat.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p126/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p126/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p126/r3.claim: The plural عجاف is an anomalous pattern for أعجف/عجفاء, analogized to سمان; only a small set of adjectives show this pattern.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p126/r3.anchor: وهي شاذة حملوها على لفظ سمان فقالوا: سمان وعجاف،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p126/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p126/r4.speaker: ابن السكيت
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p126/r4.claim: Ibn al-Sikkīt transmits from al-Farrāʾ variants with kasra in عجف and several comparable forms.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p126/r4.anchor: على أن ابن السكيت (¬5) قد حكى عن الفراء: عجف وحمق ورعن وخرق، بالكسر في هذه الأربعة،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p126/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p126/r5.speaker: ابن دريد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p126/r5.claim: Ibn Durayd defines عجف as thick bones stripped of flesh.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p126/r5.anchor: وقال # ابن دريد (¬1): العجف غلظ العظام وعراؤها من اللحم.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p127/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p127/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p127/r1.claim: The meaning of أفتوني and استفتاء was discussed earlier in the commentary on al-Nisāʾ.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p127/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: {أفتوني} ذكرنا معنى الإفتاء والاستفتاء في سورة النساء (¬2).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p127/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p127/r2.speaker: الأزهري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p127/r2.claim: The verb عَبَرَ for interpreting a dream comes from crossing to the far bank: an interpreter considers the dream's two sides and traces it from beginning to end.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p127/r2.anchor: وحكى الأزهري (¬3): أن هذا مأخوذ من العبر وهو جانب النهر، ومعنى عبرت النهر والطريق، قطعته إلى الجانب الآخر،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p127/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p127/r3.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p127/r3.claim: Aḥmad b. Yaḥyā calls the lām in للرؤيا a lām of attachment and reads the sense as “if you are interpreters of the dream.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p127/r3.anchor: فأما اللام في قوله {للرؤيا} فقال أحمد بن يحيى (¬4): أراد إن كنتم للرؤيا عابرين،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p127/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p127/r4.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p127/r4.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī treats the lām as emphatic; another analysis gives it the sense “toward,” directing interpretation toward the dream.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p127/r4.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري (¬5): دخلت اللام مؤكدة مفيدة معنى التأكيد، وقيل: إنها أفادت معنى إلى،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p127/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p127/r5.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p127/r5.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the lām introduces the object to clarify the meaning of interpreting.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p127/r5.anchor: وقال الزجاج (¬1): هذه اللام أدخلت على المفعول للتبيين، لمعنى إن كنتم تعبرون وعابرين،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p127/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p127/r6.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p127/r6.claim: The verb is used as an adjective meaning interpreters, as in 4:90 and 3:7; elsewhere an adjective can replace a verb, as in 7:193.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v12p127/r6.anchor: وقال صاحب النظم: وضع الفعل هاهنا موضع النعت كقوله {أو جاءوكم حصرت صدورهم} [النساء: 90]

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:41-44/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:41-44/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:12:41-44/r4.claim: The king dreamed of seven fat cows eaten by seven lean ones and seven green ears of grain alongside dry ones.

ELMALILI:12:43-44/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:12:43-44/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:12:43-44/r1.claim: The king convenes a large body of leading scholars and sages to hear his troubling dream.
ELMALILI:12:43-44/r1.anchor: meşhur ulemâ ve hukemâsının a‘yânından mürekkeb büyük bir heyet toplamış

ELMALILI:12:43-44/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:12:43-44/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:12:43-44/r2.claim: His request for a ruling means the dream is important to him and he wants its interpretation to resolve his difficulty.
ELMALILI:12:43-44/r2.anchor: bu rüya, benim için pek mühim bir mesele oldu, bunu tâbir edip müşkilimi hallediniz

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:43/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:43/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:43/r1.claim: The king is identified as one of six Hyksos rulers who ruled Egypt from 1700 to 1580 BCE after entering through Sinai; historians’ ‘shepherd kings’ label suggests they were Syrian Arabs not yet settled before conquering Egypt.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:43/r1.anchor: ülkede milâttan önce 1700’den 1580’e kadar hüküm süren altı Hiksos kralından biri olduğu bildirilmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:43/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:43/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:43/r2.claim: The Hebrews may share origins with the Hyksos: Hebrews descended from nomadic tribes that migrated from Arabia through Mesopotamia to Syria; Joseph’s favor later enabled Israelites to become an ethnic and cultural community in Egypt.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:43/r2.anchor: İbrânîler de daha önce Arabistan yarımadasından Mezopotamya’ya, sonra Suriye’ye göç eden bedevî kabilelerden birinin soyundan gelmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:43/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:43/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:43/r3.claim: By Moses’ time the Hyksos era had ended and a Coptic Pharaoh ruled Egypt, killing Israelite boys and sparing girls out of fear of their threat (2:49).
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:12:43/r3.anchor: artık Mısır’ı Kıptî soyundan gelen Firavun yönetiyordu. Ülkesi için bir tehlike oluşturacağı endişesiyle İsrâiloğulları’nın erkek çocuklarını öldürüyor, kız çocuklarını hayatta bırakıyordu

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Two inmates’ dreams and Joseph’s correct interpretations ultimately create the opportunity for him to interpret the reigning king’s dream, after which the king entrusts him with control of the kingdom.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: He does so and the interpretation proves to be absolutely true. Ultimately, this paves the way of he interpreting the dream seen by the reigning king.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: When God wills a plan, its means begin to arise on their own, however unlikely it may seem.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: its means and resources start coming into being out of their own accord.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The king considered his dream significant and suspected his naive courtiers could not interpret it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The king regarded this dream to be very significant.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The dream suppresses the second half of its image: the dry ears consume the green ears, as verse 48 clarifies; the translation supplies the omission.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: seven dry ears were eating away the seven green ones.

TABATABAI:12:6#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:6#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:6#2/r1.claim: Dream interpretation appears in Jacob’s explanation of Joseph’s dream, Joseph’s interpretation of his own, his companions’ and the king’s dreams, and in waking predictions taught by God.
TABATABAI:12:6#2/r1.anchor: ما حكاه الله تعالى من بيان يعقوب تأويل رؤيا يوسف عليه السلام

TABATABAI:12:44/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:12:44/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:12:44/r2.claim: The Egyptian king asks his council to explain a dream of seven fat cows eaten by seven thin cows, alongside seven green ears and others dry.
TABATABAI:12:44/r2.anchor: وقال ملك مصر لملئه إني أرى في منامي سبع بقرات سمان يأكلهن سبع بقرات مهازيل

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p192/r7.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p192/r7.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p192/r7.claim: The word ruʾyā is read with tafkhīm or imālah; imālah signals that its final alif is feminine because it corresponds in form to tāʾ.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p192/r7.anchor: يقرا بالتفخيم والإمالة فالحجة لمن فخم أنه أتى به على الأصل

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p192/r8.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p192/r8.speaker: الكسائي
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p192/r8.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reportedly makes imālah in this ruʾyā but opens the word in ruʾyāka; this is mistaken if meant to distinguish case, but sound if showing both permissible dialects.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p192/r8.anchor: وروي عن الكسائي أنه أمال هذه وفتح قوله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p265/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p265/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p265/r8.claim: Saman is the familiar noun and verbal noun from samina; samīn is its active participle, an irregular pairing of forms.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p265/r8.anchor: السمن: معروف وهو مصدر سمن يسمن، واسم الفاعل سمين، والمصدر واسم الفاعل على غير قياس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p265/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p265/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p265/r9.claim: Al-ʿajfāʾ describes an extremely emaciated female animal.
